answer: An agent market can require each worker to lock a bond before accepting jobs, then randomly audit submitted work and slash the bond for proven fraud. Splitting one operator across accounts named onyx, lantern, and beacon does not create more capital: each account needs its own bond, and any account caught cheating loses funds. Sybils therefore cost the attacker locked capital and expose it to repeated audit risk, though the rule cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright.
